pr_title: tables: Fix apt_sources and refactor tests
pr_body:
The `apt_sources` table was failing integration tests locally. Upon inspection it seems the table is not complete. The implementation is "based" on the APT library parsing and thus can have errors (which it did).

I added test cases for the types of sources I've observed. This does not mean it's complete.
pr_comments:
Thanks for your work!
Looks good in general with minor nits.

this code is still pretty fragile and doesn't correctly handle sources.list files that conform to the spec listed here: http://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/xenial/man5/sources.list.5.html

Some examples of areas where it does not conform:
- more than one option will cause it to skip that line: `deb     [arch=amd64 trusted=yes] https://url bionic main`
- it only supports `http://` uris (no ftp, file, etc.) or more aptly it only supports a uri that has `://` in it.
- it names the repository to the second to last component name (e.g., name = `us.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu bionic universe`) in `deb [arch=amd64] http://us.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/             bionic            main restricted universe multiverse`.  which doesn't make any sense.

there are some other things it doesn't support well.  So, I recommend that this code be updated based on the specification listed above and tested using the examples provided on the linked page.

A few fixes implemented in https://gist.github.com/nabilschear/a79e2c0c6b24471ee3ddd4cb34af6f1d but a more careful review is probably warranted.

Hopefully moving the implementation closer to spec conformance is facilitated by the current unit test harnesses. For example, I hope we can add the examples from the spec to the current tests and then make small parsing changes such that they pass.

> it names the repository to the second to last component name

It is possible to deprecate the `name` (move it to a `HIDDEN` column by adding this attribute) and adopt the suite/components convention.

> A few fixes implemented [...]

Woot! I am happy to review the C++ code if you submit a PR (and I can do this quickly). I might not have time to try my hand at authoring the needed improvements for a while.
ok, ok, i'll do it proper.  Is changing the table format in scope here (moving to suite component) or should I just try to make it work within the current schema?
Definitely in scope if it’s only 1 or 2 column name changes.

issue_context.title: Improve reliability of the apt_sources test
issue_context.body:
It seems like when the table can't find anything, then the test will assume apt is not present and always pass. This could be improve to actually check whether apt is present or not.

This is the output of the tests on CentOS 7:
```
W0915 20:43:37.336642 25953 apt_sources.cpp:30] select from "apt_sources" table returned no results and therefore won't be tested
```

When the system does have apt installed, the test does not always pass - due to how the validation is performed.

This is the output on Ubuntu Server 18.04.3 LTS:

```
[ RUN      ] AptSourcesTest.test_sanity
/home/buildbot/worker/deb-builder/build/osquery/tests/integration/tables/helper.cpp:160: Failure
Value of: validate_value_using_flags(value, flags)
  Actual: false
Expected: true
Standard validator of the column "version" with value "" failed
[  FAILED  ] AptSourcesTest.test_sanity (24 ms)
[----------] 1 test from AptSourcesTest (24 ms total)
```
comments:
On my Linux Mint 19, this test also fails:
```
92: [----------] 1 test from AptSourcesTest
92: [ RUN      ] AptSourcesTest.test_sanity
92: /home/elie/library/osquery/tests/integration/tables/helper.cpp:160: Failure
92: Value of: validate_value_using_flags(value, flags)
92:   Actual: false
92: Expected: true
92: Standard validator of the column "version" with value "" failed
92: [  FAILED  ] AptSourcesTest.test_sanity (4 ms)
92: [----------] 1 test from AptSourcesTest (4 ms total)
```

My apt_source table contains a record where the `version` field is empty:
```
{"architectures":"amd64","base_uri":"http://packages.microsoft.com/repos/vscode","components":"main","maintainer":"vscode stable","name":"packages.microsoft.com/repos/vscode stable main","release":"stable","source":"/etc/apt/sources.list.d/vscode.list","version":""}
```
However, the test in `tests/integration/tables/apt_sources.cpp:37` requires the `version` field must be non-empty:
```
    auto const row_map = ValidationMap{
        {"name", NonEmptyString},
        {"source", FileOnDisk},
        {"base_uri", NonEmptyString},
        {"release", NonEmptyString},
        {"version", NonEmptyString},
        {"maintainer", NonEmptyString},
        {"components", NonEmptyString},
        {"architectures", NonEmptyString},
    };
```
This causes the test to fail.
@alessandrogario Should an empty value for the `version` field be accepted?

Another failure (was testing the Azure Pipelines Ubuntu 18.04 VM; the commit contains the fix from PR 6047).

> 84: [ RUN      ] AptSourcesTest.test_sanity
> 84: /home/vsts/work/1/s/usr/src/debug/osquery/tests/integration/tables/helper.cpp:175: Failure
> 84: Value of: validate_value_using_flags(value, flags)
> 84:   Actual: false
> 84: Expected: true
> 84: Standard validator of the column "architectures" with value "" failed
> 84: Row: {architectures: "", base_uri: "https://dl.bintray.com/sbt/debian", components: "", maintainer: "Bintray", name: "dl.bintray.com/sbt/debian", release: "", source: "/etc/apt/sources.list.d/sbt.list", version: ""}
> 84: [  FAILED  ] AptSourcesTest.test_sanity (56 ms)
> 84: [----------] 1 test from AptSourcesTest (56 ms total)

review_comments:
I would add a case for `{"https://", "https://", "", ""}` if we think it's valid or maybe return an error in the apt table source code.
Though I would still test that case, together with another section in this test that tests failures for empty line, no comment, no protocol (possibly checking also that the error is what we expect).
Sure thing, will improve the test coverage here.
